exchange-operand: the replacement `e` of `move loc with e` (0174) — a named owned binding, a fresh producer, a borrow, a `using var`, and an `e` that consumes or kills the holder
routes.rule: §28.8.1 (0174): "The replacement `e` is an owned value for the location's declared type" | "a borrow is rejected, as it is at any store into an owned location" | "and so is a `using var`" | "the receiver and the index are operands of the `move`, evaluated before `e` and used at the exchange, so a consume of the holder binding inside `e` is frozen as at a call's receiver" | "leaves the location unchanged; a replacement already produced is an unbound owned temporary disposed by the unwind" | "The exchange itself runs no user code and disposes nothing"
routes.cite: §28.8.1 (*The replacing `move`*, proposal 0174), K3.1, K5 clause 5, §28.6, axiom A5, §28.3 (unbound owned temporaries); tracker #5923
routes.note: New route (0174). The replacement sits at K3.1's marker-free store position: a fresh producer or `move` result is stored, a named owned binding is left moved-from (frozen), a borrow is rejected as at any owned store, and a `using var` is rejected (A5). An `e` that consumes the holder binding is frozen as at a call's receiver; an exception in the receiver, index, `e` or the checks leaves the location unchanged and disposes the replacement as an unbound temporary. Hunted `move _r with new Wrap(_r)` (the replacement holds a borrow of the displaced value in a non-owned field): the constructor's store of its plain parameter is the field-store residual, and the taker's later disposal of the old value is K5.6's overwrite posture, as `_r := new Wrap(_r)` already is (there the overwrite disposes it at once); flag-backstopped in checked mode. No escape found.

routes.route: exchange: a borrow of a field's or slot's current value, live across a replacing `move loc with e` that displaces it (same body, or through a borrowed receiver in a callee), the taker then disposing the displaced value
routes.rule: §28.8.1 (0174): "A borrow of the displaced value taken before the exchange is bounded afterwards by the taker, under the posture every field or slot overwrite already has" | §28.8.1 (0174): "The receiver `x` in `move x.f` is any object expression — `this`, a parameter, a local holder, an element borrow (`move pool[i].Child with fresh`) — whose field `f` is `owned` and accessible at the site" | "fields and slots are not frozen" | §28.2: "any instance member access on a logically-disposed instance — an instance method call (including interface and virtual dispatch), a property or indexer accessor invocation, or a field access through the reference — raises `DisposedAccessException`"
routes.cite: §28.8.1 (*The replacing `move`*, 0174; #5695), K5.6, K4.3 (domain clause), K4.1, §28.2 (checked mode), §28.7; tracker #5923
routes.note: New route (0174). `var b := h._r; Swap(h); b.N();` with `Swap(p: Holder)` doing `var old := move p._r with new Res(); old.Dispose();`, or the same exchange in one body: the borrow `b` of the displaced value is bounded afterwards by the taker under the posture every field or slot overwrite already has — fields and slots are not frozen (K5.6), the domain clause is recorded (K4.3), and the read faults as `DisposedAccessException` in the default checked build (K4.1). The borrower may exchange exactly when it may overwrite (#5695), so the route adds no posture `p._r := new Res()` lacks. No static bound, as before; admitted-bounded by the flag.

routes.route: exchange-await: `move loc with e` whose `e` suspends (`move this._box.R with await MakeAsync()`), the receiver evaluated before the `await` and used at the exchange; the holder overwritten or disposed during the suspension
routes.rule: §28.8.1 (0174): "the receiver and the index are operands of the `move`, evaluated before `e` and used at the exchange, so a consume of the holder binding inside `e` is frozen as at a call's receiver" | "run when `e` has been evaluated, immediately before the exchange, so nothing `e` does (a call that resizes the collection or empties the field, a suspension at an `await`) can invalidate them" | "fields and slots are not frozen" | §28.2: "any instance member access on a logically-disposed instance — an instance method call (including interface and virtual dispatch), a property or indexer accessor invocation, or a field access through the reference — raises `DisposedAccessException`"
routes.cite: §28.8.1 (0174: order, checks after `e`), K9.5, K5 clauses 5–6, K4.1, §28.2 (checked mode), §30.1; tracker #5923
routes.note: New route (0174). A holder binding consumed inside `e` is frozen (a compile error). A field-path receiver (`this._box`) is a borrow of the field's current value held across the `await`: another task's overwrite of `_box` during the suspension disposes the old box, and the exchange's field access through the stale receiver is "a field access through the reference" on a logically-disposed instance, raising `DisposedAccessException` in checked mode before the store — the location unchanged, the replacement disposed by the unwind; undefined in an unchecked build, the posture of every K5.6 borrow (a call receiver held across an `await` argument, `this._box.Put(await MakeAsync())`, is the same shape and predates 0174). The bounds, key and `!` checks run after the `await`, so a resize during the suspension cannot misplace the store. Admitted-bounded by the flag.

routes.route: own-typed-slot: a record that holds borrows reaching its own-typed `Equals` slot (0176) through a boxed receiver, `Object`'s surface, an interface conformance, a type parameter or the equality search
routes.rule: §9.2 (0176): "Through the slot — a boxed receiver, or `Object`'s surface reached with an argument that is not a `T`, `null` included — the member runs only on a `T` payload and any other argument compares unequal without the body running" | §9.2: "No value kind declares a member at `Object?`, so no `T`-typed argument is boxed to reach one" | §8.6: "So a value that holds borrows ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)) is converted to `Object` or to an interface type at exactly **one position**" | §11.2: "Interface members are implicitly public, have no body, and end with `;`" | stdlib §4: "A value kind's member for the first kind is its own-typed `Equals`, declared or generated, its `Object` slot, and no value kind declares an `Equals` at `Object?` (spec §9.2), so the search never boxes a value that holds borrows."
routes.cite: §9.2 (Dispatch modifiers on value kinds; Through a type parameter), §8.6, §9.7 (borrow-erasing bullet), §11.2, stdlib §4 (equality search); proposal 0176; tracker #5924; #5916 (open, context)
routes.note: New route (0176). The record's own-typed `Equals(other: Pair)` is its `Object` slot. Every way to reach it boxes nothing that holds borrows: `p.Equals(q)` passes `q` at `Pair`; `p.Equals(o)` at `o: Object?` boxes only the receiver (the one admitted position) and runs the body only when `o` is a boxed `Pair`, which no conversion can produce; an interface conformance would need the record converted to the interface (borrow-erasing), and interface members have no body that could read `this` at the interface type; `where T: hashable` calls reach the slot at `T`. #5916 (open) asks whether a value kind may satisfy an interface member `Equals(other: Object?)`: under either answer its argument is `Object?`, never a box of a record that holds borrows. Rejected wherever a borrow would be boxed; no escape found.

routes.route: no-common-type: a member meant to accept "any read-only span" after 0175 — two overloads, `SequenceEqual` across backings, or a parameter typed `Object`, an interface or a type parameter
routes.rule: stdlib §4.16 (0175): "A member that accepts a read-only span of either heap backing declares two overloads, `(ReadOnlySpan<T>)` and `(ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>)`, each the direct-dispatch path" | stdlib §4.14: "`SequenceEqual` is declared on each span type for its own type and for the read-only span of each heap backing" | §9.7: "A value that holds borrows may not reach a **borrow-erasing position**" | §9.7: "`b.Keep<Object>(span)` over `Keep<T>(x: T)`; `xs.Add(span)` at `xs: Array<Object>`" | §12.7: "A test in which a **type parameter** stands on either side — a carrier `v: T` or `v: T?`, or a target `T` — is decided **per instantiation**"
routes.cite: stdlib §4.14, §4.15, §4.16 (retired stub, proposal 0175), §3.3; §9.7 (borrow-erasing bullet; generic-body paragraph); §12.7; tracker #5921
routes.note: New route (0175). With no common interface, a member over either backing declares two overloads (each a plain span parameter, bounded as any record parameter), and `SequenceEqual` compares across backings by overload, never by boxing. A user trying to unify the two at `Object` or an interface is rejected at the conversion (borrow-erasing); at a type parameter the requirement is read per instantiation (`Keep<ReadOnlySpan<int>>` storing into a `T` field rejected wherever named). Admitted at the record overloads, rejected at every reference-typed unification. No escape found.

routes.route: where-class: a dispatched generic `async` body under `where T: class` (0175 flip: it now establishes holds-no-borrows), its `T` parameter live across `await`, at a class, interface, `string` or function-type substitution
routes.rule: §30.1 (0175): "a compile error unless the declaring method's constraints establish that the parameter's type holds no borrows" | §30.1 (0175): "a class bound, `where T: class` or `where T: sendable` does" | stdlib §4.16 (0175): "no reference type is read as holding borrows, and a value that holds borrows converts to `Object` or an interface only as the receiver of a member call" | §28.3 Set-erasing positions: "at an instantiation substituting a function type or `Object`, nullable or not, for it" | "every borrow source reaching an async call must outlive the settlement of the returned task"
routes.cite: §30.1 (dispatched-body clause), §14.2 (dispatched generic methods; `where T: class`), §3.6 (holds-borrows: value types only), §28.3 (Set-erasing positions; argument contributions), stdlib §4.16 (0175); tracker #5816 (note), #5921
routes.note: New route (0175). `where T: class` admits classes, interfaces, `string` and function types, and holds-borrows is a property of value types only, so after 0175 removed the one reference type read as holding borrows the flip is sound: a class or interface argument is an ordinary borrow held to settlement (no interface value can box a value that holds borrows, the receiver being the only boxing position); a function-typed argument at the bare-`T` parameter is a set-erasing position at the caller, so a capture-bearing closure is rejected at the call and a capture-free one carries nothing; a `string` carries nothing. Conditional on the caller-side settlement obligation; no escape found.
